disputed: Timeline correction: the Florida library removals were driven by state laws signed by Gov. DeSantis (HB 1467 in 2022, HB 1069 in 2023), not by Trump's first term (2017-2021). Supporters describe most removals as parents' rights and age-appropriateness reviews of sexually explicit material, not censorship, and say PEN America's definition of a 'ban' (including temporary removals pending review) inflates the count. Supporters of the Ten Commandments laws argue the texts are historical documents, and the 5th Circuit agreed they don't violate the First Amendment, although opponents say this contradicts the Supreme Court's 1980 Stone v. Graham decision. The administration argues returning education to states improves outcomes. The long-term effect on student achievement is not yet measurable.

items: PEN America counted 6,870 school book bans in 2024-25, with Florida (2,304), Texas (1,781) and Tennessee (1,622) accounting for about 80%, and nearly 23,000 since 2021 across 45 states. Utah and South Carolina created statewide 'no read' lists. (Fox 4 / PEN America (https://www.fox4news.com/news/pen-america-banned-book-report-2025); PEN America (https://pen.org/book-bans/pen-america-index-of-school-book-bans-2024-2025/))

Jan 24, 2025: the Education Department's Office for Civil Rights dismissed 11 book-ban complaints, called book bans 'a hoax,' eliminated the 'book ban coordinator' position, and ended its civil-rights agreement with Forsyth County (GA) schools. (School Library Journal (https://www.slj.com/story/Department-Education-Office-Civil-Rights-Dismisses-Book-Ban-Complaints-ends-agreement-forsyth-county))

After Trump's executive orders on 'gender ideology' and 'divisive equity ideology,' Pentagon-run schools for military families (DoDEA) removed about 596 titles on slavery, Native American and women's history, LGBTQ topics and sexual-harassment prevention, plus parts of AP Psychology. On Oct 20, 2025 a federal judge ordered the books returned at the five schools in the suit. (ACLU (https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/dodea-must-return-books-to-shelves-judge-rules); Military Times (https://www.militarytimes.com/news/your-military/2025/10/22/judge-orders-immediate-return-of-books-removed-from-5-dod-schools/))
sections.label: Documentation - book removals

items: Executive Order 14190, 'Ending Radical Indoctrination in K-12 Schooling' (Jan 29, 2025), threatens federal funding for schools that teach the US is 'fundamentally racist, sexist or otherwise discriminatory,' targets 'gender ideology' and 'discriminatory equity ideology,' and re-establishes Trump's first-term 1776 Commission for 'patriotic education.' (Georgetown Free Speech Project (https://freespeechproject.georgetown.edu/tracker-entries/trump-executive-order-targets-education-seeks-to-boost-patriotism-and-end-indoctrination/); Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/02/03/2025-02232/ending-radical-indoctrination-in-k-12-schooling))
sections.label: Documentation - curriculum

items: Texas and Louisiana require the Ten Commandments in every public classroom. The full 5th Circuit upheld Louisiana's law 12-6 in February 2026 and Texas's on April 21, 2026, setting up likely Supreme Court review. Oklahoma has pursued Bible-related mandates. (PBS NewsHour (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/appeals-court-rules-texas-can-require-public-schools-to-display-ten-commandments-in-class); Houston Public Media (https://www.houstonpublicmedia.org/articles/education/2026/04/21/549758/texas-ten-commandments-5th-circuit-court-2/))
sections.label: Documentation - religion in public classrooms (state level)

items: Staff fell from about 4,200 (2024) to 2,300 (2026). More than 100 programs have moved to other agencies: K-12 programs to Labor, family engagement to HHS, and student loans to Treasury. The budget proposes a 35% cut to the Office for Civil Rights. McMahon: the mandate is 'to sunset a 46-year-old, $3 trillion failed federal education bureaucracy.' (OPB/NPR (https://www.opb.org/article/2026/05/14/linda-mcmahon-again-defends-dismantling-the-education-department/))
sections.label: Documentation - dismantling the Education Department

summary: The mass school-library book removals (led by Florida under DeSantis) came mostly after Trump's first term, starting in 2021-22. Trump's first term produced the 1776 Commission and its 'patriotic education' push. In the second term the federal government moved from standing aside to taking part: it called book bans a 'hoax,' ordered an end to 'indoctrination' in schools under threat of funding cuts, removed hundreds of books from military-base schools, and is dismantling the Education Department. At the same time, states are putting the Ten Commandments and Bible-based material into public classrooms.
title: Schools and libraries: book bans, 'patriotic education,' religion in classrooms, and dismantling the Education Department
